#Mean survival + growth at each site at each month, per treatment 
```{r}

#order sites on x-axis 
plots$site <- factor(plots$site, levels = c("Nanat", "Dixon", "Ellis S", "Ellis N", "Ed King", "Taylor"))

#SURVIVAL #####################################################################
plots$month <- factor(plots$month, levels = c("April", "May", "June", "August"))

plot <- ggplot(plots, aes(x = site, y = kelp_survival, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +  # Side-by-side boxplots
  facet_wrap(~ month, scales = "fixed", ncol = 1) +         # Stack facets vertically
  labs(
    x = "Site",
    y = "Kelp Survival (%)",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("open" = "#076fa6", "caged" = "#FF5733")) +  # Custom colors
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +  # Set y-axis range
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 25),  # Increase y-axis labels size
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 25),  # Increase x-axis title size
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 25),   # Increase y-axis title size
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), 
     strip.text = element_text(size = 25)  # Increase facet titles (month) size
  )

plot

#save
ggsave("/Users/tessarehill/Dropbox/MSc/Exclosures/plots/kelp_survival/survival_site_month.png", plot = plot,  width = 15, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

#Boxplot + Barplot of survival and growth, in open v cage, run t-test
```{r}

#SURVIVAL #####################################################################
#run t-test
#shapiro-Wilk test for normality, p less than 0.05, normally distributed
shapiro.test(plots$kelp_survival[plots$treatment == "caged"]) #normally distributed 
shapiro.test(plots$kelp_survival[plots$treatment == "open"]) #normally distributed 

#check variances, if the p-value from Levene’s test is greater than 0.05, you can assume that the variances are equal, and the assumption is met. 
leveneTest(kelp_survival ~ treatment, data = plots) #p = 0.781

#t-test to compare kelp survivorship between treatments
t_test_result  <- t.test(kelp_survival ~ treatment, data = plots) #p = 0.7812
t_test_result
  #mean in caged = 14.6%, mean in open = 13.58%

p_value <- formatC(t_test_result$p.value, format = "e", digits = 2)

#visualize 
plot <- ggplot(plots, aes(x = treatment, y = kelp_survival, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +  # Side-by-side boxplots
  labs(
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Kelp Survival (%)",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("open" = "#076fa6", "caged" = "#FF5733")) +  # Custom colors
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
  axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 14),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),  # Increase y-axis labels size
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),  # Increase x-axis title size
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),   # Increase y-axis title size
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1.5,  # Midpoint between two treatment groups
    y = max(plots$kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE) + 5,  # Adjusted Y position
    label = paste("p =", p_value),
    size = 5,
    hjust = 0.5
  )

plot

ggsave("/Users/tessarehill/Dropbox/MSc/Exclosures/plots/kelp_survival/surv_open_v_caged.png", plot = plot, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300)

#bar chart 
#calculate mean and standard deviation for each treatment
summary_stats <- plots %>%
    group_by(treatment) %>%
    summarise(
        mean_surv = mean(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_surv = sd(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
        n = n(),  # Sample size
        se_surv = sd_surv / sqrt(n)  # Standard error
    )

summary_stats

# Create the bar chart with mean and standard error
plot <- ggplot(summary_stats, aes(x = treatment, y = mean_surv, fill = treatment)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(), width = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbar(
        aes(
            ymin = pmax(mean_surv - se_surv, 0),  # Ensure lower bound is zero
            ymax = mean_surv + se_surv
        ),
        width = 0.2,  # Width of the error bar
        color = "black",
        position = position_dodge(0.7)
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Kelp Survival by Treatment",
        x = "Treatment",
        y = "Kelp Survival (%)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("caged" = "#FF5733", "open" = "#076fa6")) +
    theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),  # Increase title size
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20),  # Increase x-axis text size
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),  # Increase y-axis text size
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),  # Increase x-axis label size
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold")  # Increase y-axis label size
    )


plot

ggsave("/Users/tessarehill/Dropbox/MSc/Exclosures/plots/kelp_survival/bar_surv_open_v_caged.png", plot = plot, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

#Difference in survivorship by site 
```{r}

#summarize survivorship by site for open and caged plots 
surv_summary <- plots %>%
  group_by(site, treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_survival = mean(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_survival = sd(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_survival = min(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_survival = max(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()  # Number of observations
  )

#plotting the summarized data
plot <- ggplot(surv_summary, aes(x = site, y = mean_survival, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +  # Bar plot
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(mean_survival - sd_survival, 0), 
                    ymax = mean_survival + sd_survival), 
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.25) +  # Error bars
  labs(
    x = "Site",
    y = "Mean Kelp Survival (%)",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("open" = "#076fa6", "caged" = "#FF5733")) +  # Custom colors
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

plot 

#plotting with standard error (rather than standard deviation)
kelp_summary <- plots %>%
  group_by(site, treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_survival = mean(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_survival = sd(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    se_survival = sd_survival / sqrt(n)
  )

plot <- ggplot(kelp_summary, aes(x = site, y = mean_survival, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +  # Bar plot
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(mean_survival - se_survival, 0), 
                    ymax = mean_survival + se_survival), 
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.25) +  # Error bars
  labs(
    x = "Site",
    y = "Mean Kelp Survival (%)",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("open" = "#076fa6", "caged" = "#FF5733")) +  # Custom colors
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

plot 

ggsave("/Users/tessarehill/Dropbox/MSc/Exclosures/plots/kelp_survival/survival_by_month_se.png", plot = plot, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

#Is there a difference in kelp survivorship across sites (irrelevant of treatment)?

#assess normality - histogram 
ggplot(plots, aes(x = kelp_survival, fill = site)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, alpha = 0.7, position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ site) +
  labs(title = "Kelp Survival Distribution by Site") +
  theme_minimal()

#Statistically test for differences 
#check for normal data using Shapiro test 
plots %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(shapiro_p_value = shapiro.test(kelp_survival)$p.value) #all normal

#run Levene's test for homogeneity of variance, if P < 0.05, significantly different variances
levene_result <- leveneTest(kelp_survival ~ site, data = plots)
levene_result #significantly different variances

#Run Welch's ANOVA for kelp survival across sites
welch_anova_result <- oneway.test(kelp_survival ~ site, data = plots, var.equal = FALSE)
welch_anova_result #significant differences between sites, p = 0.0007222

#which sites are most different from each other (Post Hoc pairwise comparison)
#post-hoc pairwise t-tests (with Welch's correction) after significant ANOVA
pairwise_result <- pairwise.t.test(plots$kelp_survival, plots$site, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
pairwise_result #no significances between sites

#no significance?? post-hoc pairwise comparisons show that, despite the overall significance from the ANOVA, the individual differences between sites are not significant when the Bonferroni correction is applied, which accounts for multiple testing.

#Kruskal test
kruskal.test(kelp_survival ~ site, data = plots) #p = 0.01

#Dunn test 
dunn.test(plots$kelp_survival, plots$site, kw = TRUE, label = TRUE) 
  #Dixon + Ellis S (0.0234)
  #Ellis S + Ellis N (0.0040)
  #Nanat + Ed King (0.0076)
  #Nanat + Ellis S (0.0006)
  #Taylor + Dixon (0.0195)
  #Taylor + Ellis N *0.0039)
  #Taylor + Nanat (0.0008)
```

```{r}
# Histogram for each site to assess normality
ggplot(plots, aes(x = kelp_growth, fill = site)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, alpha = 0.7, position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ site) +
  labs(title = "Kelp Growth Distribution by Site") +
  theme_minimal()

#check for normal data using Shapiro test 
plots %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(shapiro_p_value = shapiro.test(kelp_growth)$p.value) #all normal

# Run Levene's test for homogeneity of variance, if P < 0.05, significantly different variances
levene_result <- leveneTest(kelp_growth ~ site, data = plots)
levene_result #significantly different variances

#run Welch's ANOVA for kelp growth across sites
welch_anova_result <- oneway.test(kelp_growth ~ site, data = plots, var.equal = FALSE)
welch_anova_result #significant differences between sites, p = 0.002392

#which sites are most different from each other (Post Hoc pairwise comparison)
# Post-hoc pairwise t-tests (with Welch's correction) after significant ANOVA
pairwise_result <- pairwise.t.test(plots$kelp_growth, plots$site, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
pairwise_result #only significant difference between site = Nanat (this is an important finding to me)

#Kruskal test
kruskal.test(kelp_growth ~ site, data = plots) #p = 0.0002152

#Dunn test 
dunn.test(plots$kelp_growth, plots$site, kw = TRUE, label = TRUE) 
  #Ellis N + Ed King (0.0140)
  #Ellis S + Ellis N (0.0025)
  #Nanat + Ellis S (0.0004)
  #Taylor + Dixon (0.0083)
  #Taylor + Ellis N (0.0005)
  #Taylor + Nanat (0.0001)



```

```{r}
shapiro_results_surv #normal

dunn_surv
```

#Looking at GRAVEL SIZE effect on growth and survival
```{r}
#SURVIVAL #####################################################################
#run t-test
#shapiro-Wilk test for normality, p less than 0.05, normally distributed
shapiro.test(plots$kelp_survival[plots$gravel_size == "small"]) #normally distributed 
shapiro.test(plots$kelp_survival[plots$gravel_size == "large"]) #normally distributed 

#check variances, if the p-value from Levene’s test is greater than 0.05, you can assume that the variances are equal, and the assumption is met. 
leveneTest(kelp_survival ~ gravel_size, data = plots) #unequal - perform Welche's t-test

#t-test to compare kelp survivorship between treatments
t_test_result  <- t.test(kelp_survival ~ gravel_size, data = plots, var.equal = FALSE) #p = 01.47e-11
t_test_result
  #mean in large= 25.1%, mean in small = 3.04%

p_value <- formatC(t_test_result$p.value, format = "e", digits = 2)

#visualize 
plot <- ggplot(plots, aes(x = gravel_size, y = kelp_survival, fill = gravel_size)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +  # Side-by-side boxplots
  labs(
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Kelp Survival (%)",
    fill = "Gravel Size"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("small" = "#62a4ea", "large" = "#eacf62")) +  # Custom colors
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
  axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 14),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),  # Increase y-axis labels size
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),  # Increase x-axis title size
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),   # Increase y-axis title size
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1.5,  # Midpoint between two treatment groups
    y = max(plots$kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE) + 5,  # Adjusted Y position
    label = paste("p =", p_value),
    size = 5,
    hjust = 0.5
  )

plot

ggsave("/Users/tessarehill/Dropbox/MSc/Exclosures/plots/gravel_size/surv_smallvlarge.png", plot = plot, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300)


#barplot 
#calculate mean and standard deviation for each treatment
summary_stats <- plots %>%
    group_by(gravel_size) %>%
    summarise(
        mean_surv = mean(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_surv = sd(kelp_survival, na.rm = TRUE),
        n = n(),  # Sample size
        se_surv = sd_surv / sqrt(n)  # Standard error
    )

summary_stats

# Create the bar chart with mean and standard error
plot <- ggplot(summary_stats, aes(x = gravel_size, y = mean_surv, fill = gravel_size)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(), width = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbar(
        aes(
            ymin = pmax(mean_surv - se_surv, 0),  # Ensure lower bound is zero
            ymax = mean_surv + se_surv
        ),
        width = 0.2,  # Width of the error bar
        color = "black",
        position = position_dodge(0.7)
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Kelp Survival by Gravel Size",
        x = "Gravel Size",
        y = "Kelp Survival (%)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("small" = "#62a4ea", "large" = "#eacf62")) +
    theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),  # Increase title size
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20),  # Increase x-axis text size
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),  # Increase y-axis text size
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),  # Increase x-axis label size
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold")  # Increase y-axis label size
    )
```
